lines.text: In Hollywood sci-fi movies, exploding starships make deafening roaring booms, but in real space, there is zero sound.
Sound cannot travel without a physical medium to carry its vibrations.
On Earth, sound travels when vibrating vocal cords or speaker cones bump neighboring air molecules together.
Deep space is a near-perfect vacuum containing only a handful of hydrogen atoms per cubic meter.
With no atmospheric molecules to bump into each other, sound waves simply cannot propagate.
Even if a gigantic supernova exploded right next to your spaceship window, you would hear absolute dead silence.
In outer space, the famous tagline is true: no one can hear you scream.
